title: Orion Digital Repurchases One Million Shares
summary: Orion Digital press release: Orion Digital Repurchases One Million Shares
body_markdown:
*Cumulative share repurchases since 2022 equivalent to approximately 11% of shares outstanding*


Orion Digital Corp. (NASDAQ: ORIO; TSX: ORIO) (“Orion Digital” or the “Company”) today announced that on November 10, 2026, it repurchased one million shares of its common shares under the Company’s previously announced Nasdaq share repurchase authorization, at an average of US$1.15 per share, representing approximately 4% of the common shares outstanding as at September 30, 2026. Following this transaction, the Company has approximately US$5.7 million remaining under the authorization.


The Company intends to continue to evaluate opportunities to repurchase its common shares when it believes prevailing market prices represent an attractive use of capital. Including this most recent transaction, the Company has repurchased 1,245,725 common shares in 2026. Since 2022, the Company has repurchased common shares equivalent to approximately 11% of its common shares outstanding as at September 30, 2026.


“We remain focused on allocating capital where we believe it can generate attractive long-term returns for shareholders,” said Greg Feller, President and CFO. “At current levels, we believe opportunistic share repurchases represent an attractive use of capital given the underlying value and opportunity we see in the business.”


In its recently reported Q3 2026 financial results, the Company generated $2.5 million of operating cash flow and repaid $4.3 million of debt. Orion Digital ended September 30, 2026 with $30.9 million in cash, restricted cash, marketable securities and investments.

## **About Orion Digital Corp.**


Orion Digital Corp. (NASDAQ: ORIO; TSX: ORIO) is a financial technology company operating two platforms: a Canadian consumer platform spanning Intelligent Investing and Mogo Lending, and Carta Worldwide, its European payments infrastructure platform.


Intelligent Investing is building a capital-allocation system for an AI investing world, designed to help individual investors make better long-term investment decisions rather than simply trade more. By combining AI-powered research and analysis with portfolio context, structured decision-making and ongoing performance evaluation, Intelligent Investing aims to help investors make more informed capital-allocation decisions over time.


Mogo Lending provides Canadian consumer lending products, managed for risk-adjusted returns and capital efficiency. Carta Worldwide provides payments infrastructure supporting more than $11 billion in annual payment volume and reaching more than four million end users through its clients.


Orion allocates capital across its businesses based on expected returns, capital efficiency and liquidity requirements.
